protocol_source: docs/dx7-chip-plan-v0.1-2026-09-20.md section 6: low/mid/high notes, several velocities, short plucks, long holds, release, chords and applicable controllers
commitment: Fixed, deterministic phrase set (U01). Events are oracle events.txt lines: '<pos> <cmd> <args...>' with positions as absolute sample offsets at 48 kHz. The set is committed here and never improvised per candidate, so renders are comparable across sounds.
dry_rule: Renders are dry: no per-candidate gain normalization, no time-warping, no per-render effects. The tool records peak levels; it never alters them.

phrases.description: Low register (MIDI 36, C2) at velocity 100: exposes bass-range tuning, operator tracking and low-key envelope behavior.
Middle register (MIDI 60, C4) at velocity 100: the reference anchor every candidate is heard at first.
High register (MIDI 84, C6) at velocity 100: exposes top-key scaling, aliasing-prone ratios and operator level limits.
Middle C at low velocity 32: a quiet sound at one velocity is not automatically broken; this exposes velocity sensitivity curves.
Middle C at medium velocity 80: the middle point of the velocity response.
Middle C at maximum velocity 127: exposes velocity-sensitivity saturation and level headroom.
100 ms pluck at middle C: attack character and fast envelopes; the long tail after note-off shows release behavior.
3 s hold at middle C: exposes envelope sustain levels, slow EG segments, LFO drift and feedback stability.
0.5 s note followed by a long silent-on-keyboard window: the release tail (R4) is heard in full after key-up.
Three-note chord (C4-E4-G4) at velocity 100: exposes voice allocation and per-note phase interaction in the mono-per-note oracle render.
Held middle C with mod-wheel (CC1) swept 0 to 127 in steps: exposes LFO pitch-mod depth routing while a note sustains.
Held middle C with pitch bend swept center, up to +max, back through center to -max, then recentered: exposes bend range and phase continuity.
